claim: With alignment at 2 and every other rule off, a flock in which every bird sees every other reaches near-total agreement within 600 steps.
derivation: This is the brief's example 'alignment 2, others 0 ⇒ agreement → 1 within K steps', with the flock made well mixed so K can be derived: on a 16 × 16 torus the farthest two birds can be is √128 ≈ 11.31 < R = 12, so every bird sees all 23 others (E1, E2).
E3 then gives v′_i − V̄ = (1 − k)(v_i − V̄) with k = w_a Δt · N/(N − 1) = (2/60)(24/23) = 0.034783, where V̄, the mean velocity, is conserved while no clamp acts.
Deviations from V̄ shrink by (1 − k)^t, and 0.965217^600 ≈ 6e-10, so every heading points along V̄ well before step 600 unless |V̄| is vanishingly small.
For 24 random headings at speed 2.7, |V̄| < 1e-4 has probability about 3e-8 per seed; v_max = 8 and a_max = 50 are never reached (|a| ≤ 2 · 5.4 = 10.8).

A bird whose velocity passes near zero on its way to V̄ is lifted to v_min = 0.05 in the same direction, which does not change the heading it converges to. So directionalAgreement > 0.99 at step 600 for every seed.
